_about: Barnaby's lines as ElevenLabs v3 reads them: the same words as cues.json (captions and alignment use the plain text), with audio tags for delivery and CAPITALS for the one word that carries a line. A butler: composed, warm, quietly witty; tags are light, never theatrical.
06: [politely] Twenty-three endpoints, sir. I've taken the six that only read — [dryly] nobody's given me any keys yet.
12: Five bikes due tomorrow. Only Anika's is a problem — her brakes need TWO pairs of pads, and we've one left.
14: I can't order parts myself yet — [helpfully] but Theo built the system a way to. Shall I take that on?
16: Ten pairs from Madison, at six pounds fifty a pair. [politely] Shall I?
19: I'll need to text her and mark it ready. [politely] May I?
23: [thoughtfully] That's three bikes handed back, and the SAME four steps each time. Shall I make it one?
27: [pleased] Tom's been texted, and it's marked ready.
29: The system can't tell me — there's no report for it. [fondly] Theo always meant to write one.
30: [gently] I could write it… if you like.
32: [reassuringly] With your say-so. I'll work on a copy — nothing changes until you've seen it.
33: [pleased] Done. It adds up each mechanic's hours, the way Theo's notes count them. [reassuringly] It only reads, and all of Theo's checks still pass. Shall I add it?
35: [politely] That one needs your click, Martin. [lightly] I don't change the system on a WORD.
37: Dev's carrying thirty-one hours against his twenty. [thoughtfully] Priya starts tomorrow — shall I give her the two wheel builds?
40: [dryly] Guilty. Dev had thirty-one hours booked. You had NONE.
42: Your jobs, the parts they need, who's collecting what. [warmly] And Theo left you a note: [amused] never trust the stock count on a FRIDAY.
45: [crisply] Thirteen endpoints, sir — and two deadlines in dispute. Shall I flag them?
49: [a little proud] Twenty-eight endpoints. It's on the big card, and three jobs are queued.
